    M* — effective institution count of the world‑model row

    The Barabási–Albert size whose expected metric matches the real institution graph, per metric, pooled over the AI axis, for each structure experiment that carries a world‑model row. Left of the dashed line the real graph behaves like a smaller, better‑buffered field.

    Method

    Definition. Let f(M ; x) be the expected metric on a Barabási–Albert graph of M institutions at AI‑parameter x (N fixed at 11,322), and μWM(x) the same expectation on the real institution graph. The BA‑equivalent size M* solves f(M* ; x) = μWM(x).

    Model & priors. Each cell mean over 32 replicates has a Normal(ẏ, s²) posterior with s = sd/√32 (flat prior, 32 df — the t / χ² correction is negligible). A flat prior on the shape of f beyond monotonicity in M — justified mechanically (more institutions → smaller peer pools) and borne out by the point estimates — enforced by isotonic regression. A flat prior on M* over the sampled range [132, 425].

    Posterior. 8,000 Monte‑Carlo draws: sample the BA tail means and μWM from their Normal posteriors, isotonic‑fit f, solve f(M*) = μ̃WM by linear interpolation. Those draws are p(M* | data). The dot is E[M*], the whisker its 95 % central credible interval, the open tick the median.

    Signal gate. An x‑value enters the pool only if the BA curve's spread across M clears both replicate noise (signal / noise > 3) and 3 % of the metric's dynamic range in this experiment. A row for which no x‑value qualifies is drawn as “no M‑gradient”.

    Caveats. One graph realisation, one calibration (topology swap only — graphSource and institutionSizing changed, nothing else), the final recorded tick. This compares this world‑model graph against BA specifically; it is not a statement about real graphs in general. Wide intervals reflect that only a handful of x‑columns carry a steep enough M‑gradient to pin M* tightly.
